title.rendered: How to fix “Call Failed” error on iPhone (14 Easy solutions)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why calls fail in the first place: Most of the time, it’s your iPhone struggling to stay connected to the cellular network—signal drops, SIM glitches, or even a software bug can trip it up.
  • Trouble usually boils down to these: Weak signal, overloaded cell towers, bad SIM cards, outdated iOS, wrong settings, or hiccups from your carrier can all play a part.
  • Quick first move: close the Phone app: Force quitting and reopening it helps clear any momentary bugs. Simple, but it often works.
  • Signal check trick: Airplane Mode refresh: Walk to a stronger signal spot or toggle Airplane Mode on and off. Both give your iPhone a fresh shot at a better connection.
  • When all else fails, go deeper: Try updating iOS, turning off Wi-Fi calling, checking for carrier updates, or resetting network settings. Keep that last one handy.

There you are, about to make an important call when your iPhone suddenly flashes the dreaded “Call Failed” message. Your heart sinks, and frustration kicks in. What went wrong?

Don’t worry—you’ve landed in the right place! Below, I’ve listed quick and easy ways to fix the “Call Failed” error on iPhone, so you can get back to your conversation without a hitch.

Table of Contents
  • What does "call failed" mean on iPhone?
  • How to fix "Call Failed" on iPhone: 14 Proven solutions
    • 1. Force close the Phone app
    • 2. Check your Cellular signal
    • 3. Force restart your iPhone
    • 4. Turn off Wi-Fi calling
    • 5. Check for carrier settings updates
    • 6. Enable automatic network selection
    • 7. Select the correct network mode
    • 8. Dial *#31# to reset call settings
    • 9. Check your SIM settings
    • 10. Remove and reinsert the SIM
    • 11. Update your iPhone
    • 12. Reset Network Settings
    • 13. Check if you're been blocked
    • 14. Factory reset as a last resort
  • Video: 7 Ways to Fix Call Failed on iPhone
  • Still seeing "Call Failed"? Contact your carrier

What does “call failed” mean on iPhone?

When your iPhone keeps showing a “Call Failed” message, it usually means the device couldn’t maintain a connection with the cellular network. This could be due to a wide range of issues—from a weak signal to software bugs or SIM card problems.

Common reasons why your iPhone says “Call Failed”:

  • Poor cellular reception: If you’re in an area with low or no signal, your call might not go through.
  • Network congestion: High traffic on your carrier’s network can lead to temporary connection drops.
  • SIM card issues: A damaged or improperly inserted SIM card can block outgoing calls.
  • Software glitches or outdated iOS: Bugs and outdated system software may affect call performance.
  • Call settings misconfigured: Features like Airplane Mode, Do Not Disturb, or call blocking may interfere.
  • Carrier-related problems: Service disruptions or unpaid bills can lead to call restrictions

How to fix “Call Failed” on iPhone: 14 Proven solutions

Before diving in, try calling the number again—it might have been a one-time issue. If that doesn’t help, follow these steps:

1. Force close the Phone app

Start by force closing the Phone app. This simple trick can eliminate app-related glitches:

  1. Swipe up from the bottom of the screen to open the App Switcher.
  2. Swipe up on the Phone app to close it.

  3. Reopen the app and try making the call again.

2. Check your Cellular signal

If you’re in a low-signal area, try moving to a different spot. To refresh your network connection:

  1. Open Control Center (swipe down from the top-right).
  2. Toggle Airplane Mode ON → wait a few seconds → turn it OFF again.

3. Force restart your iPhone

Rebooting your iPhone can fix temporary software bugs:

Follow our step-by-step guide to hard reboot your iPhone

4. Turn off Wi-Fi calling

Wi-Fi calling can sometimes conflict with mobile calls:

  1. Go to Settings → Cellular → Wi-Fi Calling.
  2. Toggle off Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone.

You can also find it under Settings → Phone → Wi-Fi Calling.

5. Check for carrier settings updates

Installing the latest carrier update can improve call connectivity:

  1. Go to Settings → General → About.
  2. Wait a few seconds. If an update is available, you’ll see a prompt to install it.

6. Enable automatic network selection

Let your iPhone automatically choose the best available network:

  1. Go to Settings → Cellular → Network Selection.
  2. Toggle on Automatic.

Already enabled? Try disabling it briefly and choosing a network manually, then switch it back to automatic.

7. Select the correct network mode

Using the wrong network type can cause call drops:

  1. Go to Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data.
  2. Choose 5G, 4G, or LTE, depending on what your carrier supports.
  3. Disable VoLTE if you’re using older network types.

8. Dial *#31# to reset call settings

You may have accidentally hidden your caller ID. To reset:

  1. Open the Phone app → tap the Keypad.
  2. Dial *#31# and hit the Call button.
  3. A confirmation message will appear—tap Dismiss.

9. Check your SIM settings

Using dual SIM? Make sure you’ve selected the correct one for calls:

  1. Go to Settings → Cellular → Default Voice Line.
  2. Choose the appropriate SIM for making calls.

To set a default SIM for specific contacts:

  1. Open a contact in the Phone app.
  2. Tap always use → select your SIM → tap Done.

10. Remove and reinsert the SIM

If you haven’t taken out your SIM in a while, try this:

  • Use the ejector tool to remove the SIM.
  • Wipe it gently with a soft cloth.
  • Reinsert the SIM card securely.

For eSIM users:

  1. Go to Settings → Cellular.
  2. Tap the eSIM → select Delete eSIM.

  3. Then, tap Add eSIM to set it up again.

11. Update your iPhone

Keeping your iOS version up to date can resolve many bugs:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Tap Download and Install if an update is available.

12. Reset Network Settings

This will reset all network-related configurations:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.


    ‍ 
  2. Tap Reset → Reset Network Settings.
  3. Enter your passcode → Confirm reset.

Note: This will erase Wi-Fi passwords, Bluetooth pairings, and VPN settings.

13. Check if you’re been blocked

A call that fails instantly could mean the other person blocked your number. Try calling a different contact, or read our guide on how to tell if someone blocked you.

14. Factory reset as a last resort

Only do this if all else fails:

  1. Back up your iPhone using iCloud or Finder.
  2. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  3. Tap Erase All Content and Settings.
  4. Tap Erase All Content and Settings.
  5. Follow the on-screen steps to restore.

Video: 7 Ways to Fix Call Failed on iPhone

Still seeing “Call Failed”? Contact your carrier

If none of the above fixes helped, reach out to your mobile service provider. They can:

• Check for outages in your area.

• Replace a faulty SIM card.

• Ensure your plan is active and has no pending bills.

Still stuck? Contact Apple Support and book a Genius Bar appointment to check for hardware issues.

Wrapping up…

There’s nothing more frustrating than your iPhone refusing to make a call when you need it the most. Hopefully, one of these 14 fixes for the iPhone “Call Failed” error helped you out.

Which solution worked for you? Let us know in the comments!

FAQs

Why does my iPhone keep saying “Call Failed” even with full signal?

This could be due to network congestion, SIM card issues, software bugs, or incorrect settings like a blocked number or hidden caller ID.

Can a bad SIM card cause “Call Failed” on iPhone?

Yes. A damaged or malfunctioning SIM can interfere with call connectivity.

Does iOS update fix call issues?

Yes, updating to the latest iOS version can resolve known bugs and improve overall performance.

  • What does Cancelled Call mean on iPhone and how to fix it!
  • What is call waiting on iPhone and how to activate it
  • iOS 18 call recording not working on iPhone? 4 ways to fix

mainEntity.name: How do I activate Accessibility Reader on my Apple device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings (or System Settings on Mac) > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Accessibility Reader, then turn it on.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I find Accessibility Reader in my Settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure your device is running iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS Tahoe 26 (or later). It’s not available in older versions.

mainEntity.name: Can Accessibility Reader read from images or PDFs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It works with any visible text on the screen, including PDFs and images opened in supported apps.

mainEntity.name: How does Accessibility Reader work with VoiceOver?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works alongside VoiceOver, giving you a cleaner text view while VoiceOver reads the content.

mainEntity.name: Is the Accessibility Reader available in all apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works in most apps that display selectable text, but results can vary in apps with locked or highly customized layouts.

mainEntity.name: How do I change the reading voice or language?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Voices to choose a different voice or language.

mainEntity.name: What privacy controls are in place when using Reader?

acceptedAnswer.text: All processing happens on-device. Your text is never sent to Apple servers.

mainEntity.name: Does Accessibility Reader work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It doesn’t need the internet for reading or customization.

mainEntity.name: How to use Accessibility Reader in school or work settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pair it with Magnifier to read whiteboards, presentations, or documents in real time.

mainEntity.name: What do I do if Accessibility Reader is not working after an update?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restart your device, check Accessibility settings, or ensure the feature is enabled again after the update.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can adjust fonts, spacing, and colors to match your reading needs.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore my Mac without Time Machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can restore specific files using iCloud or perform a full restore using a disk clone. Data recovery tools may also help if no backups exist.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore only certain files instead of the whole system?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, both Time Machine and iCloud support selective file recovery. Disk clones usually restore the entire system, but you can manually copy files.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: What if my backup isn’t showing up?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your backup isn’t showing up, make sure your Time Machine drive is properly connected and functional - run Disk Utility if necessary. For iCloud, check your internet connection and verify that you’re signed in with the correct Apple ID. If you’re using a disk clone, ensure the external drive is bootable; if problems continue, contact the software provider or Apple Support.

aioseo_meta_data.description: Tired of the "Call Failed" error on your iPhone? Check out these 14 easy fixes to restore your calls and avoid interruptions. Works for iPhone 13, 14, 15 and more.

blockGraphs.question: Why does my iPhone keep saying “Call Failed” even with full signal?
blockGraphs.answer: This could be due to network congestion, SIM card issues, software bugs, or incorrect settings like a blocked number or hidden caller ID.

blockGraphs.question: Can a bad SIM card cause "Call Failed" on iPhone?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. A damaged or malfunctioning SIM can interfere with call connectivity.

blockGraphs.question: Does iOS update fix call issues?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, updating to the latest iOS version can resolve known bugs and improve overall performance.

keyPoints.title: Meaning of 'Call Failed' Message on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: It indicates the device couldn't maintain connection with the cellular network, often due to signal issues, software bugs, or SIM problems.

keyPoints.title: Common Causes of 'Call Failed' on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Poor reception, network congestion, SIM card issues, outdated iOS, incorrect call settings, or carrier problems can all trigger the error.

keyPoints.title: Simple Fix: Force Close the Phone App
keyPoints.explanation: Closing and reopening the app can resolve glitches that may be causing call failures.

keyPoints.title: Enhance Signal: Check Cellular Reception and Toggle Airplane Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Moving to a better signal area and toggling Airplane Mode refreshes network connection and can fix the problem.

keyPoints.title: Update and Reset Settings to Fix Call Failures
keyPoints.explanation: Updating iOS, checking carrier updates, turning off Wi-Fi calling, resetting network settings, or updating network mode can improve call reliability.

title.rendered: How to Use the Shortcuts App on iPhone and iPad (2026 Guide)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What shortcuts actually do: They’re basically automated mini-programs built from actions that handle tasks like messaging, opening apps, or even combining steps into one tap. iOS 26 gives them an extra push.
  • Pre-made options to save time: You’ll find a bunch of ready-to-go shortcuts in the Gallery or App Library. Just download, tweak a few settings, and you’re good.
  • Build your own flow: Want something unique? Pick your actions, set the order, and pop that shortcut onto your Home Screen or widget stack. Makes a difference when it’s yours.
  • New AI touches in iOS 26: Apple added things like text summaries and smart replies right into Shortcuts. It’s subtle but really handy once you try it.
  • Works across devices, but be mindful: You can run shortcuts via the app, Siri, Share Sheet, or widgets on iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch. Just make sure each device supports the actions you’ve picked.

Shortcuts on iPhone are truly a game-changer when it comes to keeping productivity up and making simple tasks a little easier. You can automate repeated actions, create simple workflows, and even tap into Apple Intelligence features.

Whether you’ve never tried Shortcuts before or are looking to take your automation game to the next level, this is your step-by-step guide on how to use the Shortcuts app on iPhone and iPad.

Table of Contents
  • What Are Shortcuts and Actions?
  • How to Find and Use Pre-built Shortcuts
  • How to Create a Custom Shortcut on iPhone
  • Using Apple Intelligence Features in Shortcuts (iOS 26)
  • How to Run a Shortcut on iPhone or iPad
  • Use Widgets for Quick Access
  • How to Run a Shortcut on Apple Watch
  • How to Create an Automated Shortcut
  • How to Manage and Organize Your Shortcuts
  • How to Share Shortcuts with Others
  • Must-Try Shortcuts for iPhone Power Users
  • Troubleshooting Common Issues
  • Work Smarter, Not Harder with iPhone Shortcuts

What Are Shortcuts and Actions?

Shortcuts are mini-programs that automate tasks on your iPhone or iPad. You can think of them as quick commands that combine multiple steps into a single tap or voice command. Each shortcut is made up of actions, which are individual steps. Actions do things like send a message, play music, or open an app.

For example, here’s a shortcut that combines the following actions:

  • Turn on Do Not Disturb
  • Set an alarm for 7:00 AM
  • Play your morning playlist

With iOS 26, shortcuts have never been more powerful. You can combine multiple Apple Intelligence actions into a single shortcut and run it from your iPhone or even with Siri. This level of integration opens up many possibilities to improve your efficiency and automate experiences for yourself, your family, or your business.

How to Find and Use Pre-built Shortcuts  

Pre-built shortcuts are workflows that are already created and available for you to download and use immediately. These are great if you don’t want to build shortcuts from scratch. Here’s how to get started:

  1. Open the Shortcuts app. If you can’t find it, download it from the App Store. 
  2. Tap the Gallery tab to browse Apple-curated Shortcuts.  
  3. Look for categories like Morning Routine or Shortcuts for Accessibility. Tap See All to explore the category. 
  4. Select a shortcut to preview its actions and access points.
  5. Tap Set Up Shortcut to save it to your library. You can edit it later if needed.

You can also discover shortcuts based on your installed apps in the Library tab. Scroll down and tap the app to view its available shortcuts.

Tip Many third-party websites like RoutineHub provide complex and unique shortcuts. Always download from trusted sources to avoid security risks.

Once added, shortcuts appear in the All Shortcuts tab, ready to run with a tap. You can also add them to your Home Screen or widgets for quick access.

Related: How to Edit Shortcuts on iPhone

How to Create a Custom Shortcut on iPhone

If you can’t find a shortcut that fits your needs, create one from scratch. It’s easier than you think. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Shortcuts app, go to the Library tab, and tap the + button at the top right.
  2. Search for tasks like “Play Playlist,” explore the action categories at the top, or scroll to find app-specific actions. Combine multiple actions if needed.
  3. Customize each action. For example, in the Send Message action, choose a contact and type a default message or set it to paste from the clipboard.
  4. Tap the down arrow at the top, select Rename, give your shortcut a title, and tap the checkmark. You can also change its icon by selecting Choose Icon.
  5. Tap the info (i) button at the bottom, select where the shortcut should appear—like the Home Screen, Share Sheet, or Apple Watch—and tap the checkmark to save.
  6. Tap the play button to run your shortcut and confirm it works.
  7. Tap the back button at the top left to save it.

With so many available options and controls, you can create shortcuts for nearly everything.

Using Apple Intelligence Features in Shortcuts (iOS 26)

With iOS 26, Apple Intelligence supercharges Shortcuts with AI-driven actions. These allow you to interact with your iPhone in smarter ways, like summarizing text or generating quick replies.

Here’s how to use them:

  1. In the Shortcuts app, go to Gallery and explore the Apple Intelligence category.
  2. Alternatively, start creating a shortcut and search for actions like “Summarize Text” or “Generate Image.”
  3. Add additional actions and customize them according to your needs.
  4. Example: Build a shortcut that summarizes voicemails and sends the summary to your Notes app.
Note Apple Intelligence Shortcuts require an iPhone 15 Pro or later running iOS 26.

How to Run a Shortcut on iPhone or iPad

You can run shortcuts in several ways, depending on your preference:

  • Shortcuts App: Open the app, go to the Library tab, and tap the shortcut.
  • Share Sheet: In any app, tap the Share icon and select the shortcut.
  • Home Screen: Tap the three dots on a shortcut, select the info (i) button, and choose Add to Home Screen.
  • Action Button (iPhone 15 Pro or later): Go to Settings > Action Button, choose Shortcut, and select one to run with a press.
  • Siri: Say, “Hey Siri, [shortcut name]” to run it hands-free.

Use Widgets for Quick Access

Widgets make shortcuts even more accessible:

  1. Long-press your Home Screen or Today View, then tap Edit > Add Widget.
  2. Search for and select the Shortcuts widget.
  3. Swipe to choose a widget size (small, medium, or large), then tap Add Widget.
  4. For multi-shortcut widgets, long-press the widget, tap Edit Widget, and select a folder to display. 
  5. Tap the shortcut tile to run it directly from the widget.

Widgets are great for quick access to frequent tasks, such as starting a workout or checking your calendar.

Related: How to Add and Edit Widgets on Your iPhone

How to Run a Shortcut on Apple Watch 

Shortcuts on your iPhone automatically sync to your paired Apple Watch if both devices are updated.

  1. On your iPhone, open the Shortcuts app.
  2. Tap the three dots on a shortcut, select the info (i) button, and toggle on Show on Apple Watch.
  3. On your Watch, press the Digital Crown, open Shortcuts, and select one.
  4. You can also create a shortcut complication by customizing your Watch face.
Tip Use it to log water intake, start workouts, or control smart devices instantly.

You can also access iPhone shortcuts across other Apple devices. Go to Settings > Apps > Shortcuts and make sure iCloud Sync is enabled.

How to Create an Automated Shortcut 

A regular shortcut must be triggered manually, but an automation runs automatically when certain conditions are met.

Example: Trigger a shortcut to open your garage door and turn on lights when you arrive home.

Here’s how to create one:

  1. Open the Shortcuts app and tap b at the bottom.
  2. Tap the + icon at the top.
  3. Choose a Trigger, such as:
    • Time of Day: Run at a specific time.
    • Arrive/Leave: Based on your location.
    • App Opened: Triggered when an app opens.
    • System Controls: Triggered by Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or Airplane Mode.
    • Focus: Linked to a Focus mode.
    • Battery: Based on battery level or charging.
    • Sound Recognition: Triggers when iPhone hears a sound like a doorbell.
  4. Choose when the automation should run and enable Run Immediately if desired.
  5. Tap Next, select actions like Send Message or use a custom shortcut, then tap the checkmark to save.
Tip I created an automation that enables Low Power Mode when the battery hits 30%. iOS 18 also adds triggers like connecting to a specific Wi-Fi network.

How to Manage and Organize Your Shortcuts

Keep your shortcuts tidy for easier access:

  • Rearrange: Tap Edit and drag to reorder.
  • Create Folders: Select shortcuts, tap the folder icon, and create folders like Work or Home.
  • Edit: Tap the three dots to modify actions.
  • Delete: Tap Edit, select the shortcut, then tap the bin icon and confirm deletion.

Review your shortcuts regularly to remove outdated ones or update them for new iOS features.

How to Share Shortcuts with Others

Sharing allows friends or family to use your shortcuts:

  1. Go to the Library tab and tap the three dots on the shortcut.
  2. Tap the Share button and choose AirDrop, Messages, or another app.
  3. Or select Copy iCloud Link to generate a shareable link.

Always test shared shortcuts to make sure they work on other devices.

Must-Try Shortcuts for iPhone Power Users

Here are some top recommendations:

  • PhotoCollage Pro: Combine multiple photos into a grid.
  • Log Water: Track your water intake in the Health app.
  • Text Last Image: Send your most recent photo to a contact.
  • GIF Maker: Turn images or clips into a GIF with one tap.
  • Morning GPT: Read your calendar events, weather, and top news headlines.

Create a location-based shortcut that opens your shopping list when you arrive at the store.

Troubleshooting Common Issues 

If your shortcuts aren’t working, try the following:

  • Update iOS: Go to Settings > General > Software Update.
  • Check Permissions: Go to Settings > Shortcuts, then enable Private Sharing.
  • Restart the App: Force quit and reopen Shortcuts, or restart your device.
  • Simplify the Shortcut: Test each action to isolate the issue.
  • Reset Settings: If nothing works, go to Settings > General > Reset > Reset All Settings (note: this affects other preferences too).

For Apple Watch: Make sure both devices are updated and properly paired. If Siri won’t trigger shortcuts, check Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri.

Work Smarter, Not Harder with iPhone Shortcuts

Shortcuts empower you to do more with less effort. Whether it’s launching automations, using AI, or activating features hands-free, the Shortcuts app helps you simplify your day.

Start with something simple today. Set up a Siri command or try a pre-built automation. With iOS 26, your possibilities are only expanding—make your iPhone work smarter for you.

Related articles worth reading:

  • 20 Best macOS shortcuts for fast workflows
  • How to use the Shortcuts app on your Mac
  • How to merge PDFs on iPhone and iPad

mainEntity.name: Can I restore my Mac without Time Machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can restore specific files using iCloud or perform a full restore using a disk clone. Data recovery tools may also help if no backups exist.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore only certain files instead of the whole system?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, both Time Machine and iCloud support selective file recovery. Disk clones usually restore the entire system, but you can manually copy files.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: What if my backup isn’t showing up?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your backup isn’t showing up, make sure your Time Machine drive is properly connected and functional - run Disk Utility if necessary. title.rendered: Fix One AirPod Not Working – Complete Troubleshooting Guide

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why one AirPod might stop working: It often comes down to battery imbalance, Bluetooth bugs, grime, outdated firmware, or just one off audio setting. Sometimes, it’s physical damage.
  • Start with the basics: Fully charge both AirPods and the case, clean them gently, and double-check your audio balance and Bluetooth settings. That fixes a lot of common issues.
  • Still not working? Try updating your firmware, doing a hard reset, or testing on another device. Firmware’s sneaky like that—it can mess things up without warning.
  • Know when to escalate: If one pod refuses to charge, shows physical damage, or nothing else has worked, it’s time to contact Apple Support.
  • Keep things running smooth: Clean regularly, store them properly, avoid moisture, and update software. Trust me, a quick wipe now saves you later.

Apple AirPods have become a go-to for many of us because they connect effortlessly and are so easy to use—no wonder they’re such a favorite for wireless listening! But let’s be honest: even the best gadgets can run into hiccups. If you’ve ever had just one AirPod—the left or the right—suddenly stop working, you’re not alone. It can throw off your groove but don’t stress. This is a common issue, and there are several simple ways to fix it.

Below, you’ll find a friendly, step-by-step guide that walks you through everything from quick checks and easy troubleshooting to more advanced fixes. I have also included some expert tips to help you decide if it’s time to get professional help or consider a replacement. My goal is to help you understand why one AirPod is not working—and what you can do to fix it, so you can get back to enjoying your music without missing a beat!

Why is One AirPod Not Working? Common Causes

Before trying to fix the problem, it’s helpful to know what could be causing it:

  1. Battery problems: One AirPod may be out of power, not charging correctly, or its battery may be defective.
  2. Bluetooth issues: The connection between your AirPods and your device might not be working correctly.
  3. Dirt or debris: Dust, earwax, or lint can block the speaker, making one AirPod seem quiet or silent.
  4. Software or firmware bugs: Old software or firmware can cause connection or sound issues.
  5. Audio settings: Incorrect balance or mono audio settings may direct sound to only one ear.
  6. Physical damage: Drops or getting wet can harm the inside parts.

Proactive Red Flags:

Watch for early warning signs of bigger problems—like one AirPod draining battery faster, random dropouts, or taking longer to pair or charge. Addressing these issues promptly can prevent them from getting worse. With that said, here’s what to do if one AirPod is not working—starting from the basics and moving to advanced fixes.

Basic Checks and Quick Fixes

Before you panic, make sure your AirPods are charged—and not clogged with dust or earwax.

1. Ensure Both AirPods and Case Are Charged

Let’s start simple: pop both AirPods into their case and give them at least 30 minutes to recharge. Double-check that your case has enough juice and that your charging cable and adapter are plugged in and working—sometimes, it really is that easy!

How to check battery levels

  1. Hold your AirPods case close to your iPhone or iPad. A popup will appear showing the battery level of each AirPod and the case.
  2. To check more battery details, swipe right on your iPhone’s home screen to open the Today View and find the Batteries widget. If you can’t see it, scroll down, tap “Edit,” and add the Batteries widget.

If only one AirPod isn’t charging

  1. Take out both AirPods and check the charging contacts in the case and on the AirPods for any dirt or debris. Clean them gently if needed (see cleaning instructions below).
  2. If possible, try charging a different pair of AirPods in your case or place your AirPods in another case to determine if the case is the issue.
  3. If one AirPod still does not charge, it may be a battery or hardware issue—see the section below for guidance on seeking professional help.

2. Clean Your AirPods Carefully

If you notice sound problems, muffled audio, or your connection cutting in and out, it could mean your AirPods are getting dirty. Please don’t wait until one AirPod stops working to clean them.

How to inspect and clean your AirPods

  1. Check first: Look at the speaker mesh and microphone holes on both AirPods. If you see dust, earwax, or dirt, it’s time to clean them.
  2. Wipe the exterior: Gently wipe your AirPods and the charging case with a soft, dry, lint-free cloth.
  3. Clean the speaker mesh: Use a soft, dry brush (such as a clean makeup or paintbrush) or a dry cotton swab to gently remove dirt from the mesh. Don’t use liquids or sharp objects, as they can damage your AirPods.
  4. Clean the charging points: Use a dry cotton swab to clean the charging contacts inside the case and on the AirPods.
  5. If you have AirPods Pro or AirPods 4: Take off the silicone or foam ear tips, rinse them with water (never rinse the AirPods), and dry them thoroughly before putting them back on.

Myth-busting tip

Do not use compressed air to clean your AirPods. It can force debris deeper inside or damage fragile components.

How often should you clean?

  1. For daily users: once a week
  2. After workouts or heavy use: after each session
  3. If you notice muffled sound or fit issues, inspect and clean immediately

If cleaning doesn’t restore sound, continue with the next steps.

Connection and Audio Settings

Fix common connection and sound issues by repairing your AirPods, restarting your device, and adjusting audio settings.

1. Repair Your AirPods

A fresh connection of AirPods to your device resolves many issues. Here’s how:

  1. Go to Settings > Bluetooth on your device and tap the “i” next to your AirPods, then tap “Forget This Device.”
  2. Put both AirPods back in the charging case and close the lid for at least 15 seconds.
  3. Open the lid and hold the case near your device.
  4. Press and hold the setup button on the back of the case (if present) until the light flashes white.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to reconnect.
Model-specific note If you have AirPods 4 (the case has no button), open the lid and tap the front of the case twice while the light is on. Do this again when the light flashes white and one more time when it flashes faster. When the light flashes amber and then white, your AirPods are reset and ready to connect.

How to check your AirPods model

Go to Settings > Bluetooth, tap the “i” next to your AirPods, and note the model number. You can look up your AirPods model on Apple’s identification page.

2. Restart Your Device

Sometimes, the problem is with your phone, tablet, or computer. Restart your device (while your AirPods are in the case), then try to connect again.

3. Check Audio and Accessibility Settings (Balance and Mono Audio)

Wrong audio settings are a common problem—and they can change without you noticing. Accessibility features, software updates, or allowing others to use your device can all modify these settings without notice.

1. How to check and adjust

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Audio/Visual.
  2. Make sure the “Balance” slider is centered between L and R. If it’s off to one side, the sound will only play through one AirPod.
  3. Ensure “Mono Audio” is turned OFF. If Mono Audio is on, all sound will play through just one AirPod.
Pro Tip: If you use accessibility shortcuts, such as triple-clicking the Side or Home button, you may have accidentally enabled Mono Audio or other hearing features. Check these shortcuts if the issue happens again.

2. Check your stereo sound

After changing your settings, play a song or video that features clear left and right sound effects (many music apps or YouTube have test tracks available). Listen to see if the sound moves between your ears to make sure both AirPods are working.

  1. Open Settings.  
  2. Go to Accessibility.  
  3. Tap the Audio/Visual tab.
  4. Bring the slider under Balance to the center or at 0.00.

Software and Firmware Troubleshooting

Updating your device software and AirPods firmware can resolve common connectivity and audio issues.

1. Update Your Device Software

Ensure your device is up to date. Go to Settings > General > Software Update and install any available updates.

2. Check and Update AirPods Firmware

Firmware updates for AirPods are automatically downloaded and installed when they’re charging and near your device. To check your firmware version:

  1. Go to Settings > Bluetooth, tap the “i” next to your AirPods, and look for the firmware version.
  2. Compare it with the latest version on Apple’s AirPods firmware page.
  3. If you suspect an update is pending, keep your AirPods in the case, connected, and near your device.

Advanced Troubleshooting

Still facing issues? These deeper troubleshooting methods can help resolve stubborn AirPods problems.

1. Hard Reset Your AirPods (Model-Specific)

If previous steps haven’t worked, try a complete reset of your AirPods:

AirPods with case button

  1. Place AirPods in the charging case and open the lid.
  2. Press and hold the button on the back for about 15 seconds until the LED flashes amber, then white.
  3. Reconnect to your device.

AirPods 4 (no button)

  1. Open the lid and double-tap the front of the case while the status light is on.
  2. Double-tap again when the light flashes white and a third time when it flashes faster.
  3. When the light flashes amber and then white, reconnect your AirPods.

2. Reset Network Settings

If you suspect a network or Bluetooth issue:

  1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings.

Warning: This action will delete all saved Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth devices. Ensure you have your Wi-Fi passwords and are ready to reconnect your accessories.

3. Test on Another Device

To check if your original device is the problem, try connecting your AirPods to another phone, tablet, or computer. If both AirPods work on the other device, the problem might be with your original device’s settings or hardware.

When to Contact Apple Support

If you have tried all the troubleshooting steps and still have problems, it’s time to ask the experts for help. Here’s how to know when getting professional help is the best choice:

Contact Apple Support if you notice any of these

  1. One AirPod will not charge, turn on, or be recognized—no matter what you try.
  2. Persistent audio dropouts, static, or distortion that don’t improve with resets or cleaning.
  3. One AirPods battery drains significantly faster than the other, even after a reset.
  4. Visible physical damage (cracks, dents, water exposure)
  5. No sound from one AirPod despite all troubleshooting

What to Prepare Before You Call or Visit Apple Support

  1. AirPods serial number (found on the case or in device settings)
  2. Proof of purchase (for warranty or AppleCare+ claims)
  3. A quick list of the troubleshooting steps you’ve already tried
  4. A brief description of the issue and when it started
Pro Tip: Catch Problems Early!

Watch for subtle warning signs before total failure

  1. One AirPod takes much longer to pair or charge
  2. Occasional unexplained audio cutouts on one side
  3. Gradually worsening battery life on a single AirPod

Spotting these early can help you get support before the situation worsens.

What to Expect from Apple Support

  1. Remote diagnostics or in-person evaluation (at a Genius Bar)
  2. Mail-in repair or replacement options.
  3. Repairs or replacements free or discounted if under warranty/AppleCare+.
  4. Out-of-warranty service for a fee (Apple will quote you the cost)
  5. Advice on safe, authorized repairs (using third-party repair services may void your warranty!)

Need to keep listening while you wait?

Set your device to mono audio and use your working AirPod for calls or music until the problem is fixed.

In summary: If you see these warning signs, don’t keep trying the same fixes. Apple Support can help you—acting early can save you time, money, and stress.

Maintenance Tips to Prevent Future Issues

  1. Inspect and clean regularly: Check your AirPods and case for debris weekly or after heavy use. Wipe with a dry, lint-free cloth and gently brush the speaker mesh.
  2. Store properly: Always keep AirPods in their case when not in use.
  3. Avoid moisture and extreme temperatures: AirPods are not waterproof.
  4. Keep firmware and device updated: Updates can fix bugs and improve performance.
  5. Routinely check audio settings: After software updates or device sharing, quickly verify your audio balance and mono audio settings.
  6. Watch for battery decline: If one AirPods battery life drops significantly, consider service or replacement.
  7. Set a reminder: Add a recurring calendar event or phone reminder to clean your AirPods—proactive care prevents most issues.

Keep Your AirPods Working Perfectly

Most times, getting your AirPods back up and running again simply takes the form of quick troubleshooting. When you get into the habit of keeping them clean, checking the settings, and giving them the TLC they require, you’re not just getting things working—you’re getting the best out of your music and extending the life of your AirPods.

Go through these steps one at a time, and odds are you’ll be back to enjoying your favorite tunes in stereo before you know it. And if things still aren’t right, don’t worry—Apple Support has your back.

Has our tip worked, or is there a question to ask? I would love to hear from you in the comments below!

FAQs

Why does one AirPod die faster?

If one AirPod uses the microphone more or is older, its battery might run out faster. If battery problems continue, you may need to get it serviced.

Can I buy a single replacement AirPod?

Yes, but only through Apple Support—not in stores.

What if my AirPods work on another device but not mine?

The problem is probably with your device’s Bluetooth or audio settings. Try resetting the network settings or updating your device.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

keyPoints.title: Common Causes for One AirPod Not Working

keyPoints.title: Basic Troubleshooting Steps
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure both AirPods and the case are charged, clean your AirPods carefully, and check connection and audio settings to resolve many common issues.

keyPoints.title: Advanced Fixes and Firmware Checks
keyPoints.explanation: Update your device and AirPods firmware, perform hard resets, reset network settings, or test on another device if basic fixes don't work.

keyPoints.title: When to Seek Professional Support
keyPoints.explanation: Contact Apple Support if one AirPod won't charge, shows persistent issues, physical damage is visible, or other troubleshooting fails after trying all recommended steps.

keyPoints.title: Preventative Maintenance Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Regularly clean your AirPods, store them properly, avoid moisture, keep software updated, and monitor battery health to prevent future problems.

title.rendered: iPhone Is Disabled, Connect to iTunes? Here’s How to Unlock It Safely

content.rendered:
Seeing the message “iPhone is Disabled. Connect to iTunes” on your screen can feel like a nightmare. Whether it was you, your kid, or your pocket entering the wrong passcode too many times, the result is the same: you’re locked out. But don’t panic. There are ways to unlock your iPhone. However, you will lose your data unless you have a backup already. Let’s get started.

Table of Contents
  • Why Does My iPhone Say "iPhone Is Disabled. Connect to iTunes"?
  • Things to Know Before You Start
  • How to Fix "iPhone Is Disabled, Connect to iTunes" Error
    • Method 1: Use iCloud or the Find My App (No Computer Needed)
    • Method 2: Restore Using a Computer (macOS or Windows)
      • Step 1: Turn Off Your iPhone
      • Step 2: Enter Recovery Mode
      • Step 3: Restore Using Finder or Apple Devices App
    • Method 3: Use DFU Mode if Recovery Fails
  • How to Avoid This Problem in the Future
  • Final Thoughts: Regain Access and Prevent Future Lockouts

Why Does My iPhone Say “iPhone Is Disabled. Connect to iTunes”?

Apple built this lockout system to protect your data. After six wrong passcode attempts, your iPhone disables for one minute. Keep guessing, and the lock time increases: 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour. After too many failed tries (usually 10), your iPhone either disables permanently or, if you enabled it, erases itself completely.

Things to Know Before You Start

Before jumping into the recovery steps, here are a few important things you should understand. These points will help you know what to expect and avoid surprises later on:

  • You can’t unlock a disabled iPhone without erasing it.
  • That means you’ll lose data if you haven’t already backed up.
  • After wiping the iPhone, you can set it up as new or restore it from a backup.
  • You’ll need a computer or access to your iCloud account.

Many third-party tools claim to unlock your iPhone, but most are not safe to use. Stick to official methods.

How to Fix “iPhone Is Disabled, Connect to iTunes” Error

You’ll need a device that uses the same Apple ID, or you can restore using any Mac or Windows PC.

Method 1: Use iCloud or the Find My App (No Computer Needed)

If you had Find My iPhone enabled, this is the easiest way.

  1. Go to iCloud.com/find or open the Find My app on another Apple device signed in to the same Apple ID.
  2. Tap All Devices (on iCloud) or go to the Devices tab in the app.
  3. Select your disabled iPhone.
  4. Tap or click Erase This Device (or Erase) and confirm your choice.
  5. Once erased, your iPhone will restart. You can now set it up like new or restore from an iCloud backup.

Method 2: Restore Using a Computer (macOS or Windows)

If iCloud isn’t an option, you’ll need a Mac or PC with iTunes or the Apple Devices app.

Step 1: Turn Off Your iPhone

Before you can enter recovery mode, power off your iPhone completely.

  • iPhones with Face ID: Hold the Side button and Volume Down.
  • iPhones with Home button: Hold the Top or Side button.
  • Slide to power off and wait a few seconds.

Step 2: Enter Recovery Mode

Connect your iPhone to your computer using a Lightning or USB-C cable. Immediately press and hold the correct button based on your model:

  • iPhone 8 or later: Hold the Side button.
  • iPhone 7 / 7 Plus: Hold the Volume Down button.
  • iPhone 6s or earlier: Hold the Home button.

Keep holding until the recovery mode screen appears, showing a cable and computer icon.

Check out this guide for clear, step-by-step instructions on how to put your iPhone into Recovery Mode.

Step 3: Restore Using Finder or Apple Devices App

Once you’re in recovery mode, your computer will prompt the next steps:

  1. On macOS Catalina or later: Open Finder.
  2. On older Macs or Windows: Open the Apple Devices app or iTunes.
  3. Grant permission for your iPhone to connect.
  4. Select your iPhone.
  5. When prompted, click Restore iPhone, then confirm by clicking Restore again.

Once done:

  • If you have a backup, select Restore Backup and follow the on-screen instructions.
  • If not, choose Set Up as New iPhone to start fresh.

Method 3: Use DFU Mode if Recovery Fails

If recovery mode doesn’t work, DFU (Device Firmware Update) mode is your next option. This deeper restore method can help when your iPhone refuses to restore normally.

Put your iPhone into DFU mode (steps vary by model), connect it to your computer, and restore it using Finder or iTunes. This wipes everything and gives your iPhone a completely fresh start. Use it only if you’re comfortable with advanced troubleshooting.

Still Stuck? Contact Apple Support

If you’re still having trouble unlocking your iPhone, reach out to Apple Support. They can help walk you through your options and check for any hardware-related issues.

How to Avoid This Problem in the Future

Here are some practical tips to prevent being locked out again:

  • Use Face ID or Touch ID: It reduces the need to enter your passcode often.
  • Pick a memorable passcode: Avoid “1234” or “0000”. Use something secure but easy for you.
  • Enable Find My iPhone: This allows you to erase your iPhone remotely if locked out.
  • Back up regularly: Either to iCloud or your computer. If something goes wrong, at least your data is safe.
  • Disable Erase Data Option: Your iPhone might auto-erase itself after 10 wrong passcode attempts if this setting is enabled. To turn it off, go to Settings > Face ID (or Touch ID) & Passcode, scroll down, and toggle off Erase Data.

Final Thoughts: Regain Access and Prevent Future Lockouts

Getting locked out of your iPhone can be stressful, but it’s not the end of the world. Apple has built-in recovery tools that can help you regain access. Just remember, recovery means erasing your iPhone, so having a backup is critical.

And maybe, just maybe, keep your phone away from curious toddlers next time.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I repost a Story even though I was tagged?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possible reasons include: the Story expired, you’re not following a private account, or the user disabled resharing. Do they get notified when I repost? Yes. When you repost a Story you’re tagged in using Instagram’s native feature, the original poster is notified.

mainEntity.name: Can I adjust the flashlight brightness with Siri?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Siri can only turn the flashlight on or off—not adjust brightness (yet).

mainEntity.name: Why does opening the Camera app turn off the flashlight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because your iPhone's camera flash and flashlight use the same LED. Opening the Camera app disables the flashlight function.

mainEntity.name: Can I remove the flashlight from the Lock Screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, starting with iOS 18.2, you can customize or remove Lock Screen shortcuts.

mainEntity.name: Can I quickly turn off the flashlight if my screen isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes—using Siri or a Back Tap gesture can help if your touch screen is unresponsive.

mainEntity.name: Do all iPads have a flashlight?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only iPads with a rear camera flash (LED) have the flashlight feature. If you don't see the icon, your iPad likely doesn't support it.

title.rendered: Apple Launches $20 AppleCare One Plan for Multi-Device Protection

content.rendered:
If you own more than one Apple product, you’re probably juggling multiple AppleCare+ plans or skipping them altogether. But that changes now. Apple just launched AppleCare One, a new subscription that covers multiple Apple devices under a single plan. It’s simpler, more flexible, and for many users, cheaper too.

AppleCare One: New $20/Month Protection Plan

AppleCare One is a monthly subscription service that lets you protect up to three Apple devices for $19.99/month. Want to add more? You can add each extra device for $5.99/month. You get the same benefits as AppleCare+, but in one neat bundle. It supports iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, MacBook, AirPods, HomePod, Apple TV and even the Vision Pro headset.

With AppleCare One, you’re not missing out on anything. All the key protections from AppleCare+ are here:

  • Unlimited accidental damage repairs (for drops, spills, and more)
  • Battery service if your battery health drops below 80%
  • 24/7 priority support from Apple experts
  • Apple-certified repairs, including on-site or mail-in service
  • Theft and Loss coverage, now expanded to iPads and Apple Watches, not just iPhones

You can also swap devices in and out of your plan anytime. So if you trade in your iPhone, the new one can automatically take its place in your coverage.

You Can Finally Cover Older Devices Too

Previously, you had just 60 days after purchase to add AppleCare+ to a device. AppleCare One changes that. You can now add most products up to four years old, as long as they’re in good condition. Headphones, however, must be less than a year old.

To make sure a device qualifies, Apple might ask you to run a diagnostic test using your iPhone or visit an Apple Store.

How Much Can You Save?

Because the pricing doesn’t change based on device type, AppleCare One can save you money, especially if you have multiple devices. For example:

  • Covering an iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch with AppleCare+ would usually cost about $21/month. With AppleCare One, it’s just $19.99/month.
  • Add a fourth device, and you still save compared to buying separate plans. A MacBook, iPhone, iPad, and Watch setup would cost around $29/month individually, but only $25.98/month with AppleCare One.

So yes, the savings add up, but more importantly, you don’t have to manage multiple plans anymore.

What About Users in iPhone Upgrade Program?

If you’re on the iPhone Upgrade Program, your monthly payment already includes AppleCare+. Apple now says you can move that coverage to AppleCare One instead.

You’ll need to contact Apple Support to unbundle AppleCare+ from your loan, then add the iPhone to AppleCare One. This can lower your Upgrade Program payment, but the switch isn’t seamless. It may make your next iPhone upgrade a bit trickier since the system expects the bundled plan.

For most users, it’s easier to keep the included AppleCare+ and use AppleCare One for other devices. But if you’re managing multiple products, moving everything under one plan could still be worth it.

Any leftover AppleCare+ balance is refunded as an Apple Gift Card once the new plan starts.

A Few Things to Keep in Mind with AppleCare One

Before you jump in, here are some small but important limitations to be aware of. These could affect how well the plan fits your setup.

  • It’s tied to your Apple ID. Only devices signed in to your Apple account can be added.
  • No yearly payment option. It’s month-to-month only.
  • Available only in the U.S. for now.
  • Theft and Loss coverage includes up to three claims per year for iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.

When and Where Can You Get It?

AppleCare One officially launches July 24. You can sign up directly from your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or by visiting an Apple Store. If you already have AppleCare+ on your devices, you can upgrade to AppleCare One and transfer your coverage. The process is simple: go to your Apple ID > Subscriptions in your iPhone/iPad settings, choose to switch plans if you’re eligible, confirm devices, and agree to cancel your old AppleCare+ plan.

mainEntity.name: How do I activate Accessibility Reader on my Apple device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings (or System Settings on Mac) > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Accessibility Reader, then turn it on.

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure your device is running iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS Tahoe 26 (or later). It’s not available in older versions.

mainEntity.name: Can Accessibility Reader read from images or PDFs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It works with any visible text on the screen, including PDFs and images opened in supported apps.

acceptedAnswer.text: It works alongside VoiceOver, giving you a cleaner text view while VoiceOver reads the content.

acceptedAnswer.text: All processing happens on-device. Your text is never sent to Apple servers.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore my Mac without Time Machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can restore specific files using iCloud or perform a full restore using a disk clone. Data recovery tools may also help if no backups exist.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, both Time Machine and iCloud support selective file recovery. Disk clones usually restore the entire system, but you can manually copy files.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: What if my backup isn’t showing up?

keyPoints.title: Introduction of AppleCare One
keyPoints.explanation: AppleCare One is a new subscription service that simplifies coverage for multiple Apple devices under a single plan, making it more flexible and cost-effective.

keyPoints.title: Affordable Monthly Subscription
keyPoints.explanation: For $19.99 per month, Apple users can protect up to three devices, with additional devices costing $5.99 each, covering a wide range of Apple products.

keyPoints.title: Comprehensive Protections Included
keyPoints.explanation: AppleCare One offers benefits similar to AppleCare+, such as unlimited accidental damage repairs, battery service, 24/7 support, certified repairs, and expanded theft and loss coverage.

keyPoints.title: Flexible Device Management and Coverage
keyPoints.explanation: Users can add or swap devices in the plan at any time, with most products up to four years old eligible for coverage, and the process involves simple diagnostics or store visits.

keyPoints.title: Cost Savings and Practical Benefits
keyPoints.explanation: AppleCare One can save users money, especially with multiple devices, and eliminates the hassle of managing multiple insurance plans, with costs comparable or lower than separate plans.

title.rendered: Apple Just Changed App Store Age Ratings: Here’s What’s New

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • New Age Ratings: Apple added new age rating levels: 13+, 16+, and 18+.
  • Automatic Re-rating: All apps have been automatically re-rated, but developers can manually change it.
  • Developer Deadline: New required questions must be answered in App Store Connect by January 31, 2026.
  • Compliance Required: Apps must still follow COPPA, GDPR, and Apple’s content safety rules.

Apple is tightening up how it handles age ratings on the App Store. If you’re a developer or a parent keeping an eye on what your kids can access, there’s a lot changing quitely. This update is all about giving users, especially parents, a better control while nudging developers to be more responsible.

More Specific Age Ratings: 13+, 16+, and 18+ Added

Until now, App Store age ratings were pretty broad: 4+, 9+, 12+, and 17+. But that’s changing. Apple has now introduced three new age brackets: 13+, 16+, and 18+. These updated ratings are already live on devices running the latest betas of iOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, and other Apple platforms.

The new system offers more granularity and lets developers better align their apps with age-appropriate content. Importantly, these ratings vary by country based on regional content standards.

Automatic Re-Rating and Manual Overrides

Apple has already reassigned age ratings automatically using developers’ existing questionnaire responses. But if the new rating doesn’t match your app’s intended audience, you can manually change it via App Store Connect.

There’s also a new option: if your app has its own policy requiring users to be older than Apple’s rating, you can now set a higher minimum age yourself.

Apple is reminding developers to consider all app features, including AI chatbots and virtual assistants, when evaluating sensitive content. This means that even if your app looks kid-friendly on the surface, but your AI feature can surface adult or controversial topics, it needs the right rating.

Developers Must Answer New Questions by January 31, 2026

Alongside the new ratings, Apple has added four new required questions to the age rating questionnaire:

  • Does your app include in-app controls (like parental filters)?
  • Does it include special capabilities (like social sharing or account creation)?
  • Does it touch on medical or wellness topics?
  • Are there violent themes in your app or game?

These questions help Apple assign a more accurate rating. Developers have until January 31, 2026 to fill them out. After that, if you haven’t completed the form, your app updates will be blocked in App Store Connect.

Still Bound by COPPA, GDPR, and App Review Guidelines

None of this overrides Apple’s existing policies. Apps still need to follow local laws like the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) in the US, and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in the EU. App Review Guidelines also continue to apply, especially rules around objectionable and user-generated content.

In short, Apple wants the App Store to be more trustworthy – not just for parents, but for everyone. And it’s now placing more responsibility on developers to make that happen.

  • Apple’s 2025 App Store Updated Policy

mainEntity.name: Can I restore my Mac without Time Machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can restore specific files using iCloud or perform a full restore using a disk clone. Data recovery tools may also help if no backups exist.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, both Time Machine and iCloud support selective file recovery. Disk clones usually restore the entire system, but you can manually copy files.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: What if my backup isn’t showing up?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your backup isn’t showing up, make sure your Time Machine drive is properly connected and functional - run Disk Utility if necessary. If you’re using a disk clone, ensure the external drive is bootable; if problems continue, contact the software provider or Apple Support.

keyPoints.title: More Specific Age Ratings: 13+, 16+, and 18+ Added
keyPoints.explanation: Apple introduced new, more granular age brackets for apps, which are already live on the latest Apple device betas, allowing better age-appropriate content classification.

keyPoints.title: Automatic Re-Rating and Manual Overrides
keyPoints.explanation: Apps are automatically re-rated based on existing developer questionnaires, but developers can manually adjust ratings and set higher minimum ages if necessary.

keyPoints.title: Developers Must Answer New Questions by January 31, 2026
keyPoints.explanation: Developers need to update their responses to four new required questions regarding app features and content to ensure accurate age ratings before the deadline.

keyPoints.title: Compliance Still Required with COPPA, GDPR, and Guidelines
keyPoints.explanation: New age ratings do not replace existing policies; apps must still comply with laws like COPPA, GDPR, and adhere to App Review Guidelines for appropriate content.

keyPoints.title: Focus on Responsible Content and User Safety

title.rendered: Apple Wins Lawsuit Over ‘Deceptive’ 5GB iCloud Storage Limit

content.rendered:
Lisa Bodenburg sued Apple, claiming she should have received a total of 205 GB of iCloud storage: 200 GB from the upgraded plan, plus the original 5 GB free tier. Lisa argues that Apple should have given her the 5 GB of free storage that every user receives without a paid plan, along with the 200 GB of paid storage. However, the court disagreed, and she lost the case.

A Ninth Circuit panel dismissed the appeal on July 23, 2025, upholding a previous ruling that there was no breach of contract and that Apple’s communication about its paid plans contained no shortcomings or misleading language.

What She Argued?

Lisa claimed that she believed Apple’s use of terms like “more storage” meant that her 5 GB of free storage would remain intact, with the 200 GB added on top. She further argued that Apple’s marketing gives the impression of a total, not a replacement.

But her arguments failed to convince the panel. The judges pointed to Apple’s support pages and service agreement, which clearly state that users move from a 5 GB to a larger single-tier plan.

Apple’s Model Backed by Documentation

Apple, as stated on its support pages and service agreement, clearly mentions that when users upgrade, their new plan replaces the free tier; they don’t retain both.

The court, in its ruling, said that the language used by Apple, such as “change your storage plan,” clearly indicates a replacement system. That undercuts claims that Apple misled customers.

Case Closed…

Bodenburg’s case hinged on the assumption that free storage should remain alongside the upgrade; however, nothing in Apple’s documentation promises this. Thus, the court didn’t see grounds to proceed with a class action.

This dismissal leaves the iCloud+ subscription documentation untouched. It also signals that small-scale disputes over digital storage aren’t likely to make much headway in court, especially when product language is as clear as Apple’s appears to be.

Should Apple include the free 5 GB on top of paid plans, or is the current model fair? Drop your thoughts in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Can Android users access iCloud Shared Library?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It works only on Apple devices with iOS 16.1, iPadOS 16.1, or macOS Ventura or later. Android users can view shared items on iCloud.com but can't contribute or edit. Use Shared Albums for basic sharing instead.

mainEntity.name: What happens when someone leaves the Shared Library?

acceptedAnswer.text: They lose access. If they were members for more than seven days, they can download everything. Otherwise, they keep only their own content. Remaining participants are notified and the library continues.

mainEntity.name: How do I activate Accessibility Reader on my Apple device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings (or System Settings on Mac) > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Accessibility Reader, then turn it on.

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure your device is running iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS Tahoe 26 (or later). It’s not available in older versions.

mainEntity.name: Can Accessibility Reader read from images or PDFs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It works with any visible text on the screen, including PDFs and images opened in supported apps.

mainEntity.name: How does Accessibility Reader work with VoiceOver?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works alongside VoiceOver, giving you a cleaner text view while VoiceOver reads the content.

mainEntity.name: Is the Accessibility Reader available in all apps?

mainEntity.name: What privacy controls are in place when using Reader?

acceptedAnswer.text: All processing happens on-device. Your text is never sent to Apple servers.

mainEntity.name: Does Accessibility Reader work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It doesn’t need the internet for reading or customization.

acceptedAnswer.text: Pair it with Magnifier to read whiteboards, presentations, or documents in real time.

acceptedAnswer.text: Restart your device, check Accessibility settings, or ensure the feature is enabled again after the update.

mainEntity.name: Can I customize the Accessibility Reader for color blindness or dyslexia?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can adjust fonts, spacing, and colors to match your reading needs.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore my Mac without Time Machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can restore specific files using iCloud or perform a full restore using a disk clone. Data recovery tools may also help if no backups exist.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore only certain files instead of the whole system?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, both Time Machine and iCloud support selective file recovery. Disk clones usually restore the entire system, but you can manually copy files.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: What if my backup isn’t showing up?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your backup isn’t showing up, make sure your Time Machine drive is properly connected and functional - run Disk Utility if necessary. For iCloud, check your internet connection and verify that you’re signed in with the correct Apple ID. If you’re using a disk clone, ensure the external drive is bootable; if problems continue, contact the software provider or Apple Support.

title.rendered: Apple Releases iOS 26 Public Beta: Here’s What’s New

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Public Beta Release of iOS 26: Apple has released the first public beta of iOS 26, giving beta program members early access to new features ahead of the official launch.
  • How to Download iOS 26 Public Beta: Participants can install the beta by going to Settings → General → Software Update → Beta Updates and selecting iOS 26 Public Beta.
  • Design Changes and Visual Refresh: iOS 26 debuts the Liquid Glass interface with responsive icons, menus, and navigation that reflect light and movement dynamically.
  • New Features and App Improvements: Key additions include Apple Intelligence tools like Visual Intelligence and Live Translation, plus major updates to Safari, Phone, Messages, Apple Music, CarPlay, and the new Apple Games app.
  • Cautions for Beta Users: As a pre-release version, iOS 26 beta may have bugs or performance issues; it’s best not to install it on your main device.

Apple has finally released the first public beta of iOS 26. Members of Apple’s public beta program can now install and explore the next-generation software ahead of its official release.

As expected, the first public beta of iOS 26 includes all the features available in the fourth developer beta released earlier this week. A new fourth developer beta is also available for those enrolled in the developer program.

How to Download iOS 26 Public Beta

Downloading the iOS 26 public beta is simple if you’re already part of Apple’s beta software program:

  1. Open Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Tap the Beta Updates, then select iOS 26 Public Beta.
  3. Tap the Download and Install button once the iOS 26 Public Beta appears.

What’s New in iOS 26 Public Beta

Like the developer betas, the public beta update introduces the highly anticipated Liquid Glass interface, a refreshed visual style centered on transparency and movement. Icons, menus, and navigation bars now respond to light with gentle reflections and dynamic shifts. You’ll also notice pop-out menus, slimmer tab bars, and softer, rounded edges throughout the system.

Some highlights of iOS 26 include:

Apple Intelligence Features

  • Visual Intelligence: Analyze and summarize screenshots.
  • Image Playground: Create AI-generated images with ChatGPT-style prompts.
  • Genmoji: Mix two or more emoji to generate custom creations.
  • Live Translation: Available in the Messages, Phone, and FaceTime apps.
  • Wallet: Smarter alerts and enhanced order tracking.

UI and App Updates

  • Spatial Scene: Adds depth and dimension to 2D photos.
  • Safari: Refreshed navigation for easier browsing.
  • Phone app: Includes Call Screening and Hold Assist.
  • Messages app: Supports polls and fully customizable chat backgrounds.
  • Apple Music: New DJ-style AutoMix feature.
  • CarPlay: Overhauled interface with improved functionality.
  • Apple Games: A brand-new app for browsing and launching Apple Arcade titles.
  • Preview app: Now available on iPhone for the first time.

Ready to Dive In? iOS 26 Awaits

Although iOS 26 Public Beta is now available to everyone, please note that this is still a beta release. You may encounter bugs, glitches, or performance issues, and some features may be unstable. I recommend not installing it on your primary device.

Which iOS 26 feature are you most excited to try? Let us know in the comments!

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • iOS 26 vs iOS 18: Big Changes You’ll Notice Right Away
  • How to Downgrade iOS 26 Beta to 18 Without Losing Any Data
  • Hidden Accessibility Features in iOS 26 and macOS 26

mainEntity.name: Can Android users access iCloud Shared Library?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It works only on Apple devices with iOS 16.1, iPadOS 16.1, or macOS Ventura or later. Android users can view shared items on iCloud.com but can't contribute or edit. Use Shared Albums for basic sharing instead.

mainEntity.name: What happens when someone leaves the Shared Library?

acceptedAnswer.text: They lose access. If they were members for more than seven days, they can download everything. Otherwise, they keep only their own content. Remaining participants are notified and the library continues.

mainEntity.name: How do I activate Accessibility Reader on my Apple device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings (or System Settings on Mac) > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Accessibility Reader, then turn it on.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I find Accessibility Reader in my Settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure your device is running iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS Tahoe 26 (or later). It’s not available in older versions.

mainEntity.name: Can Accessibility Reader read from images or PDFs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It works with any visible text on the screen, including PDFs and images opened in supported apps.

mainEntity.name: How does Accessibility Reader work with VoiceOver?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works alongside VoiceOver, giving you a cleaner text view while VoiceOver reads the content.

mainEntity.name: Is the Accessibility Reader available in all apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works in most apps that display selectable text, but results can vary in apps with locked or highly customized layouts.

mainEntity.name: How do I change the reading voice or language?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Voices to choose a different voice or language.

mainEntity.name: What privacy controls are in place when using Reader?

acceptedAnswer.text: All processing happens on-device. Your text is never sent to Apple servers.

mainEntity.name: Does Accessibility Reader work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It doesn’t need the internet for reading or customization.

mainEntity.name: How to use Accessibility Reader in school or work settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pair it with Magnifier to read whiteboards, presentations, or documents in real time.

mainEntity.name: What do I do if Accessibility Reader is not working after an update?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restart your device, check Accessibility settings, or ensure the feature is enabled again after the update.

mainEntity.name: Can I customize the Accessibility Reader for color blindness or dyslexia?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can adjust fonts, spacing, and colors to match your reading needs.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore my Mac without Time Machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can restore specific files using iCloud or perform a full restore using a disk clone. Data recovery tools may also help if no backups exist.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore only certain files instead of the whole system?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, both Time Machine and iCloud support selective file recovery. Disk clones usually restore the entire system, but you can manually copy files.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mac restore take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring your Mac from a backup typically takes 1 to 4 hours with Time Machine, depending on the size of the backup; a few minutes for individual files via iCloud; and around 30 to 60 minutes using disk clones, which is usually the fastest method.

mainEntity.name: What if my backup isn’t showing up?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your backup isn’t showing up, make sure your Time Machine drive is properly connected and functional - run Disk Utility if necessary. For iCloud, check your internet connection and verify that you’re signed in with the correct Apple ID. If you’re using a disk clone, ensure the external drive is bootable; if problems continue, contact the software provider or Apple Support.

keyPoints.title: Public Beta Release of iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Apple has released the first public beta of iOS 26, allowing members of the beta program to explore upcoming features before the official launch.

keyPoints.title: How to Download iOS 26 Public Beta
keyPoints.explanation: Participants can easily download the beta through Settings by navigating to Software Update, selecting Beta Updates, and choosing iOS 26 Public Beta for installation.

keyPoints.title: Design Changes and Visual Refresh
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 26 introduces Liquid Glass, a new interface style emphasizing transparency and movement, with icons, menus, and navigation responding to light with reflections and dynamic shifts.

keyPoints.title: New Features and Improvements in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Highlights include Apple Intelligence features like Visual Intelligence and Live Translation, as well as updates to apps such as Safari, Phone, Messages, Apple Music, CarPlay, and the new Apple Games app.

keyPoints.title: Cautions and Tips for Beta Users
keyPoints.explanation: Since iOS 26 beta is still in testing, users may encounter bugs or performance issues and are advised to avoid installing it on primary devices to prevent potential disruptions.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

Labubu dolls are the talk of the town. These mischievous elf‑like creatures are quick to grab attention and stand out with their unique charm. If you want to stay on trend and add some quirky personality to your iPhone screen, these Labubu wallpapers are just what you need.

10 Cute Labubu Wallpapers for iPhone in 4K

Here are our 10 best Labubu wallpapers for iPhone that will make your device stand out. Explore the collection below and download your favorite one for free in 4K quality.

1. Funky Pink Labubu

This adorable wallpaper features a pink-furred Labubu with big eyes, a cheeky grin, and playful vibes. With small hearts scattered across the background, it’s the perfect mix of cute and quirky.

Download

2. Labubu on a Picnic

If you’re a nature lover, this cozy wallpaper shows Labubu enjoying a sunny picnic. Dressed in a comfy autumn sweater and carrying a cute backpack, it brings a warm, cheerful vibe to your screen.

Download

3. Colorful Labubu Gang

Download

Why have just one when you can have the entire crew? This vibrant wallpaper features the quirky Labubu gang having fun with floating bills and playful doodles.

4. Cozy Labubu Café Vibes

This heartwarming wallpaper shows Labubu and friends enjoying sweet treats and warm drinks in a cozy café setting. If you’re after an aesthetically pleasing wallpaper with cutesy vibes, this one’s for you.

Download

5. Labubu in the Spotlight

Looking for a wallpaper that complements your Dynamic Island? Set against a black background, this design features a fluffy white Labubu with a bright beam shining upwards, perfect for dark mode.

Download

6. Summer Splash Labubu

Let the summer vibes roll with Labubu joyfully floating in a sparkling blue pool. This refreshing wallpaper adds a carefree and fun mood to your display.

Download

7. Peeking Labubu Wallpaper

Prefer minimalist designs? This one features a curious Labubu peeking from the side, with sparkly eyes and a mischievous grin. It adds a touch of playful personality to your iPhone.

Download

8. Say Hi to Labubu Squad

Here’s another cute and vibrant wallpaper, featuring the Labubu group in various colorful outfits. Their playful expressions and the fun “LABUBU” title at the top bring a lively charm to your screen.

Download

9. Playful Labubu in Blue

Brighten up your display with Labubu dressed in a cozy blue bunny costume. Soft blue drips and heart shapes in the background add a cheerful, lighthearted feel.

Download

10. Labubu Peek-a-Boo Duo

At last, a playful wallpaper featuring two cute Labubus peeking through torn paper. This minimal yet fun design adds a dash of mischief to your iPhone screen.

Download

“Labubu-fy” Your iPhone!

Labubu wallpapers offer a unique combination of adorableness and quirky personality for your device. Whether you’re into cozy aesthetics, playful energy, or minimalist designs, there’s a Labubu wallpaper for every mood.

Thanks for browsing our cute Labubu iPhone wallpapers! Pick your favorite and let your screen smile with Labubu’s delightful mischief.
